## Markdown

```{python}
from majordome_build.documents import *
from majordome.utilities.markdown import *
```

### Normalize LaTeX delimiters

```{python}
doc = DocumentedClass(LatexDelimiterNormalizer)
doc.classmethods()
```

The following illustrates the use of the functionality:

```{python}
#| echo: true
sample = r"""
Inline good: \( x^2 + y^2 \)

Inline missing slash: \(a+b)

Inline missing slash close: (c+d\)

Inline parenthetized: (\(c+d\))

Inline breaking case: \( V_{IJ}^{(n)} \)

Block inline: \[ \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx ]

Fragilized block:

\[ \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx ]

I noticed that sometimes links may be fragile, like in:

![diagram showing something](assets/img/favicon-32x32.png)

What about this doubly escaped inline math: \\( \\Delta J \\) ?

\\[
W_{\\text{point}}^{(n)} = \\left( W_{AA}^{(n)} + W_{BB}^{(n)} -
      2W_{AB}^{(n)} \\right)
\\]
"""

normalizer = LatexDelimiterNormalizer()
output = normalizer.apply(sample)
display(Markdown(output))
```

### Strip Markdown links

```{python}
stripper = MarkdownLinkStripper()
markdown = r"""
This is a sample markdown with some links and images.

![An image[x]](https://example.com/image.png)

Here is a [link to Google](https://www.google.com) and
another [link to OpenAI](https://www.openai.com).
"""

cleaned, _ = stripper.apply(markdown, placeholder="<removed-link>")
print(cleaned)
```
